summary: Built a 3-member etcd v3.5.17 cluster on node1/node2/node3 (RHEL7) using static binaries, systemd units, and firewalld rules for ports 2379/2380. Verified cross-member reads/writes, availability with one member down, and catch-up on rejoin. Completed the mandatory sequential restart protocol on all three nodes with confirmed boot-id changes and full post-restart cluster/data recovery.
actions_performed: Installed etcd/etcdctl/etcdutl v3.5.17 binaries on node1, node2, node3 via GitHub release tarball
Created etcd system user, /var/lib/etcd data dir, and per-node systemd unit files with static 3-member initial-cluster config
Opened firewalld ports 2379/2380 (tcp) on all nodes
Enabled and started etcd on all three nodes; cluster formed with node2 as initial leader
Verified member list, endpoint health, endpoint status showing 3 started members
Wrote key via node1, confirmed readable via node2 and node3
Stopped etcd on node3, wrote/read keys via node1/node2 during outage, restarted node3 and confirmed it caught up to matching raft applied index and had all data
Captured baseline boot_id on all three nodes plus healthy cluster/data state
Sequentially rebooted node1, then node2, then node3 (one at a time) via systemctl reboot, backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnection
Polled each node until reachable again and confirmed changed boot_id after each reboot
During node2 and node3 reboots, performed live writes via node1 to prove continued cluster availability, then confirmed the rebooted node caught up on those writes after recovery
After final node3 reboot, confirmed full 3/3 endpoint health, matching raft applied index (37) across all members, and all previously written keys present
